correctness.rationale: Exact symmetric OU Lyapunov solution, M-matrix positivity, tree unique-path cofactor identity and pinned rooted-forest determinant formula establish polynomial comparison criterion. A standard-library standalone script exhaustively generates all 280392 Prüfer words for n=2..8, groups them into 47 canonical tree classes, compares all 733 edge pairs by exact integer arithmetic, independently tests each minor by determinant at two t values, and verifies 11/11 mixed comparisons factor into one-positive-root polynomial times one-signed remainder; no n>8 claim. The explicit two Pearson formulas and crossing at 2+sqrt(5) were reconstructed symbolically and the included checker asserts the rational-polynomial identities. Finite exact enumeration plus proved bijection/factor lemma supplies the entire finite-range classification.

originality.rationale: The identical Laplacian resolvent and forest-cofactor machinery are established in Chebotarev--Shamis, and population spatial synchrony under migration is established in Lande--Engen--Sæther and Engen et al.; these are expressly excluded from novelty. The asserted new subject is the exact *Pearson-normalized* edge comparison and sharp complete order-two-through-eight topology classification. Full primary texts on forest metrics, matrix forest theorem, Gaussian metric-graph field and two principal ecological studies were checked for stronger implication, not only title similarity. Semantic searches and statement-level comparisons with related published mathematics yielded non-covering claims. Two highly pertinent older ecological studies were only accessible in abstract, and possible stronger specialized graph-correlation comparison remains an uncertainty; neither available abstract asserts the exact classification.
residual_risks: The complete 1999 Lande--Engen--Sæther and 2000 Kendall et al. source texts were unavailable; their analytic correlation results could conceivably include an unnoticed stronger comparison.
An unindexed graph-resolvent, forest metric, Gaussian model or matrix-proximity ranking theorem may imply this small-tree classification; literature search does not prove uniqueness.
No external independent mathematical or bibliographic audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Monitoring spatial synchrony between directly connected ecological populations is a natural observable. A sharp smallest topology and exhaustive six exceptional eight-habitat shapes show a subtle structural failure of coupling-independent local synchrony ranking under otherwise perfectly homogeneous linear dynamics. Unlike a routine inverse covariance calculation, the result precisely quantifies onset for all tree structures through eight and provides a reproducible finite-network baseline for synchrony comparisons. This mathematical value does not depend on claiming immediate empirical applicability or a general result for all graph orders.
